rationale.intervention_reconstruction: The hypothesis proposes a Cr-Al alloy coating with 5–10 wt% Al, whereas the target uses a refractory high-entropy alloy (AlTiCrZrNbTa) with varying Al content (0–25 at.%). These are fundamentally different coating systems, so the intervention is a different kind of study.
rationale.condition_agreement: The hypothesis mentions subcritical water at ~300°C and high-temperature steam at ≥800°C for minutes, while the target uses isothermal steam oxidation at 1000°C for 60 min and 1100°C for 30 min. Both involve high-temperature steam, but the hypothesis lacks the target's specific temperature, time, and steam flow conditions.
rationale.mechanism_agreement: The hypothesis invokes an alumina barrier at the coating/substrate interface to inhibit Cr–Zr interdiffusion. The target's mechanism involves a composite Al2O3-TiO2-Cr2O3 surface layer suppressing oxygen diffusion, with excess Al causing intermetallics and oxide discontinuity. These are different general classes of mechanism (interdiffusion barrier vs. oxygen diffusion barrier via multi-component oxide).
rationale.outcome_agreement: The hypothesis predicts reduced Cr–Zr interdiffusion and delayed coating failure under high-temperature steam. The target predicts minimized oxidation rate and oxygen penetration with an optimal Al content, with excess Al reversing the benefit. The hypothesis focuses on interdiffusion, while the target focuses on oxidation resistance; the predicted property and direction differ.
